turns.t: Hello. My irritable bowel is flaring up again, and I've got exams in two weeks, so I'm panicking a bit.
Okay, let's see what we can do. What's your tummy doing at the moment?
Cramping and cramping. Mostly lower down. Then I'm in the toilet a lot.
When did this flare start?
I'm not sure. Maybe a week ago, or ten days? It crept up on me.
Is the stool loose or hard?
Loose, mostly. Sometimes constipated for a day, then loose again.
Any blood in the stool, or weight loss?
No blood. I've not lost any weight that I know of.
Has this happened during exams before?
Yes, every exam season. I've had IBS since I was sixteen.
Fine, that's helpful. I'd like to check your pulse, temperature and blood pressure. ~
Go ahead.
Pulse 78, blood pressure 116 over 72, temperature 36.7, oxygen 99 percent, breathing 14.
Are they all right? ~
All normal. Let me press on your tummy. Tell me if anything is sore. ~
A bit there, on the left.
Mild tenderness in the left lower abdomen, soft, no guarding and no lumps.
Is that the IBS? ~
It fits with an IBS flare brought on by stress. Nothing here worries me.
Is there anything I can take? ~
Peppermint oil capsules can ease the cramping. And a low-FODMAP diet can help for a few weeks.
What's low-FODMAP? ~
A diet that cuts out certain fermentable carbohydrates, like onions, garlic, and some fruits. I'll give you a leaflet.
Okay. I can try that. ~
How are you sleeping and eating during revision? ~
Badly, to be honest. Lots of coffee and not much food. ~
Try regular meals and less coffee. Even a short walk each day helps a flare.
I'll try. ~
I'll also arrange a blood test and a stool test, just to be certain that nothing else is going on.
Will I get the results before my exams? ~
Yes, within the week. If you're not better in two weeks, come back and we'll talk again.
Thank you, doctor. That's a relief. ~
